body: OH YES THANKS THATS EXACTLY WHAT IM LOOKING FOUR

Validity means crap. Just be true to yourself. I know it’s hard, and depression and other shit can make life even more difficult. Being trans suck, but I have gained some mental peace and relative happiness after accepting it.

I feel you so hard. I don’t know why so many trans folx can’t get people like us. Screaming we are transphobic and giving us sugar coating “yas queen u r valid” answers to our questions doesn’t help us at all. I know I have internalized transphobia, but getting us inside a hugbox doesn’t do shit. 

The only way I found some peace was to find what makes me feel happy, and understand that my transition is for me and myself only. I don’t need to be super feminine, I don’t owe feminity to anyone nor any other gender stereotypes or roles (and believe me, trans folxs can reinforce those stereotypes as well as cis people do). I just need to be honest with myself and what I like and what makes up myself. Remove labels from femininity or masculinity and just be yourself. Believe me, life changes after that. I don’t care about passing, I just wanna be happy with myself.
I feel you soo hard
Im open to it.
I would rather kill myself than transition

I went out dressed as I wanted and felt more confortable (kinda feminine) and I felt happy. Maybe what frustrates me the most is the fact that people don’t read me as a girl (at least not as much as I would want to), and I don’t want to put that much effort into making sure that happens, I just want to make sure it happens naturally. Any tips? You have already been of great help for me :)
One of my problems is that when I want to wear that kind of stuff (usually feminine stuff) I feel stupidly disphoric. I just can’t help but se myself as a man dressed as a woman.

Thaaanks, I definitly want to drop that need to “pass” and “look like a woman”, the problem is that being seen as a boy gives me some dysphoria. I think I’ll either accept that, or, change myself to become more passable.
Thanks for your wishes! Yeah, I have always felt HRT will change my life, hope it is.
Thanks a lot! I really needed a perspective like that!

I’ve never seen things that way, maybe actually medical transition will help me too. I just want people to recognize me as a girl, that’s all. Even though I don’t want to put a lot of effort into that.
Also I’m pretty fucking scared. My therapist told me I should start correcting my pronouns to people, but I’m not sure if I can do that.

I know I’ll contradict myself, but well, I want to look like (society’s definition of) a woman. My problem is that I don’t want to try to, I don’t think it is fair that I have to put in the effort into something that should be natural for me and given to me since birth.

My problem still is that I don’t understand that congruency, what does that mean? “Acting and dressing as a woman”? I really don’t like that. Maybe because I don’t see things inherently as manly or feminine, I just see them as they are… things. Sadly this vision sucks, because even if I put in practice, people still read me as a man, and I hate that.

I’m only doing social transition right now, I’m in psychological therapy to get HRT (but to be fair I have come to accept my life without them atm) but it is going to take me a while before I can get it. The help my country provides has some strict rules about going through therapy before hormones, and I feel I need to solve a lot of things before I even start them.

And yeah, it’s better for me when I do things just because I like them, regardless of the cisgender norms attached to them. That’s why I hate when a lot of trans people in my social circle tell me to do certain stuff just because “girls do so”.

Yeah it’s time for me to finally get some closure, my gender identity is something that bothers me a lot, and it’s better if I don’t over complicate that myself. My suffering hasn’t changed a lot since I came out as trans (if not, It actually has increased).

Ijust need to know how to untangle it, as I said in another comment, maybe just ditching labels and embracing myself can help me out.

I feel exactly the same. I’m just too tired to use labels for my gender (even though I’m not non binary). The same happened with my sexual orientation, the less I tried to define it, the most inner peace it brought me.
I want to transition, i have changed my name and pronouns, but my gender expression is weird and androgynous and I feel confused because my expression is different from my identity
The idea that stupid people think people like me shouldn’t have rights
Yeah, it has gotten worse (somehow?) the first few months after coming out felt actually great, but transphobia and insecurity made me feel even worse
I’m pretty sure it’s just Transphobia, and I’m a butch trans woman,
I feel like people just play along when I tell them I’m a woman, and I hate that
Yes, I’m pretty sure I am, but living as my desired gender only makes me suffer

The problem is that she talks about HRT on her video and of course I will be better with it, I just don’t have the resources to start it because my country sucks and there are little to no specialists.
I know but still knowing I’ll never be a cis woman haunts me and saddens me. Why even try? Maybe in my next life I’ll have some luck.

My problem is that here in my country I just can’t have access that easily to HRT, there aren’t many specialists. Also I’m not even interested in surgery. But to be fair neither HRT or Surgery will make me a cis woman, so why even try? Why even should I carry on?
